(If) the netherworlds and the realms were the load on one (side of the scale), hundreds of thousands, millions of them,
(even then) the worth of your ruby (the Name) could be set only if there were others (like it) on the (other) end.
From sorrows joys arise, and from joys come sorrows;
(but) what hunger can the mouth know that sings your praise?
O Nanak, you are the one fool; the rest of the world is good.
The bodies in which the Naam does not spring up come to ruin. ॥4॥
1328.1: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
For whose sake Brahma uttered the Vedas and Shankar (Shiva) gave up Maya (the world's illusion and lure),
for whose sake the Siddhas (yogis of perfect powers) turned from the world, (his) secret the gods have not found.
O Baba, one should (keep) the True One in mind and speak of the True One with the mouth; (so) one crosses over and becomes (like) the True One.
Neither enemy nor pain comes near whoever gains the Lord's wisdom.
The make (of the world) from fire, water and air: these three are servants of the Naam;
those who do not take up the Naam are thieves; they dwell in the fort of the lions (lust and the rest).
If someone does a single good deed, he boasts greatly in his mind and heart;
so many are (the Lord's) virtues, so great his goodness; he gives and does not regret it.
(O God,) those who praise you have wealth in their laps; Nanak's wealth is that same.
If anyone addresses them with respect, no summons from Jam comes (to him). ॥4॥
1328.2: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who has no beauty, no (high) caste, no (fair) face, no flesh (to give the body strength),
on meeting the True Guru (he) has found the Lord, free of Maya; (O God,) his dwelling is in your Name.
O Avadhoot (renunciate yogi), dwell on the essence (the Lord) in Sahaj,
by which you will not come into the world again.
One who has no (ritual) deeds, no (prescribed) dharma, no (ritual) purity, no rosary,
(he) has gained understanding from the Light of Shiv; the True Guru is (his) protector.
One who keeps no fast, no vow, no (learned) debate,
(he) has no care for liberation or ruin, (for) the True Guru has given (his) word.
One in whom there is neither hope nor despair, (the Guru) has given understanding to the awareness in (his) mind;
(his) essence (the soul) has met the supreme essence (God); O Nanak, (he) has gained understanding. ॥4॥
1328.3: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What that one says is accepted at (the Lord's) door,
who knows poison and Amrit both as alike.
What can one say? (You) pervade all;
whatever happens is all your will.
(In him) the Light has shone forth and pride has ended,
(to whom) the True Guru has given the Name that is Amrit.
In Kalyug (the dark age), know that one alone to have (truly) come (into the world),
(who) receives respect in the True Court.
(That) speaking and hearing (is true which) reaches the home of the Indescribable (Lord);
O Nanak, (all other) talk and chatter burns away. ॥4॥
1328.4: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(At the Guru, the pilgrim place,) the water is Amrit, and the mind bathes in (divine) knowledge; the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are gained along with it.
In the Guru's teaching are jewels and rubies; the Sikh who serves (the Guru) seeks them out and finds them.
No place of pilgrimage equals the Guru;
the Guru is himself the pool of contentment.
The Guru is a river, (its) water ever pure; meeting (him) removes the filth of an evil mind.
When the True Guru is found, the bath is complete; (he) makes gods of beasts and ghosts.
The Guru whose heart, to its very depths, is dyed in the True Name, one should call sandalwood,
by whose fragrance the plants are made fragrant; one should keep one's attention fixed on his feet.
Through the Guru the breath of (spiritual) life springs up in beings; through the Guru one reaches the house of Shiv;
O Nanak, through the Guru one merges in the True One; through the Guru one attains one's own (true) state. ॥4॥
1329.1: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(One who) by the Guru's grace reflects on (divine) learning, reading and reading (it), wins honour;
within (his) self, (his) self is lit up, (and he) has found the Name that is Amrit.
O Creator, you are my patron (jajman);
I ask of you one offering (dakhina): give (me) your Name.
(Through the Name) the five thieves (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride), running about, are held back, and pride in the mind is ended;
the vicious gaze and the evil mind flee; such is the knowledge of God.
(O God,) make self-restraint and truth (my) rice, compassion (my) wheat, attaining (you) the leaf-plate and the grain;
make good deeds the milk and contentment the ghee: such is the gift I ask.
Make forgiveness and patience the milch cow, (that the mind,) the calf, may drink (its) milk in Sahaj.
I ask for the robe of (your) praise and of effort, (that) Nanak may keep singing the Lord's virtues. ॥4॥
1329.2: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
No one has held back one who comes; how can one who goes be held back?
He alone from whom (the world) came knows (this) fully, for (it) merges in him alone.
(O God,) you alone are; waah, (wondrous is) your will.
Whatever you do, that alone surely comes to be; nothing else can be done.
As pots are tied to the chain of the Persian wheel, one empties and others are filled again,
just so is this play of the Master, as his greatness wills.
Walking the path of awareness, the sight turned back (from Maya) is lit up.
Reflect in your mind and see, O Brahm Giani (one who knows God): who is the householder, and who the renunciate?
One who entrusts (his) hope to the One whose (gift) it is, and so stays free of desire,
(and) holds him from whom (all) came to be (the Doer): O Nanak, householder or renunciate, he is approved. ॥4॥
1329.3: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who binds (his) vicious gaze with a bond, to him I am a sacrifice.
(One who) knows nothing of sin and virtue wanders astray in vain.
Utter the True Name of the Creator,
(and) there will be no turn to come (into birth) again.
(The Creator) makes the high low, and makes the low a sultan.
Those who have truly known the Knower (of all) are, in the world, the perfect and the approved.
One would go to instruct someone if he had (of himself) gone astray;
(but) the Creator himself plays out every play; rare is one who understands it so.
At dawn one should meditate on the Name through the Shabad (the Word); give up love of the world.
Nanak, the slave of (your) slaves, humbly prays: one who has lost (himself) in the world has won. ॥4॥
1330.1: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The mind is (caught in) Maya, the mind runs (after it), the mind is a bird in the sky;
(when) through the Shabad the thieves are driven out, the town (of the body) is peopled and acclaimed.
(O God,) when you protect, when you save, the capital stays whole.
Such is the jewel of the Name, the treasure that is mine;
give (me) the Guru's teaching, (that) I may cling to your feet.
The mind (now) is a yogi, the mind (now) a seeker of pleasure; the mind is a fool, unlettered;
the mind (now) is a giver, the mind (now) a beggar; (but) over the mind stands the Guru, the Creator.
Slaying the five enemies, (one) has found peace: such is reflection on God.
The One is said to be in every heart; I say (so too), (yet he) cannot be seen.
The counterfeit one is hurled down head first (into births); without the Naam honour departs.
(O God,) when you unite (me), then I stay united (with you), when it is your will.
One should not ask about caste and birth; find out (where) the house of the True One (is).
One's caste and one's honour are as the deeds one does.
The pain of birth and death is cut away; O Nanak, through the Name (one) will be set free. ॥4॥
1330.2: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Awake (as he thinks), (he) rejoices, (yet) the blind one is being robbed;
the noose is round (his) neck, and worldly toil strikes at (his) head.
In hope (he) comes, with desire (he) goes;
the warp (of his life) is tangled, (and he) has no power at all.
O Life (of the world), O Wakeful One, you (alone) are awake;
(you are) the ocean of peace, the storehouse of Amrit.
(The blind one) does not grasp what is told (him), nor does he see (for himself); (he) has done ugly deeds.
The Supreme God himself (grants) love and affection; by (his) grace greatness is gained.
Day by day comes, and (life) wastes away bit by bit, (yet) love of Maya stays in the heart.
Without the Guru (he) stays drowned and finds no resting place, as long as there is a mustard seed's worth of duality.
Day and night (the Lord) watches over beings and cares for them; joy and sorrow (come) by what was earned before.
Luckless (Nanak) begs for the alms of Truth; may Nanak receive this greatness. ॥4॥
1330.3: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If I keep silent, I am called a fool in the world;
if I speak much, my attention on you is left behind.
Error and fault (are judged) in your court;
without the Naam, what (good) conduct can there be?
(O God,) thus is the world robbed by falsehood;
the slanderer slanders (me), yet (he) is dear to me.
The one they slander knows the way (of life);
through the Guru's Shabad (he) bears the mark (of approval) at (the Lord's) door;
(he) knows the Naam, the cause (of all), to dwell within;
the one on whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, he alone knows the way.
I am soiled; the True One alone is pure.
By calling (oneself) noble, no one becomes high.
The manmukh (the self-willed) eats the great poison openly;
whoever turns Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) is steeped in the Name.
(I am) blind, deaf, foolish and unlettered,
lowly, base, bad and worst of the bad;
(but) for (me), the poor one, the wealth is the Naam and love (for the Lord);
this wealth is the best; all else, the poison (of Maya), is ash.
Praise or slander, the Shabad and reflection (on it):
hail to the One who gives (them).
(When) you forgive, (one gains) caste and honour;
Nanak speaks (as) he (the Lord) has him speak. ॥5॥
1331.1: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Eating (without the Name), one has added to (the mind's) filth; by wearing (fine clothes), one has only brought loss to one's own house;
prattling on and on, one has stirred up strife; without the Naam, know (all this) as poison.
O Baba, the mind has come to dwell in such a hard snare;
only by braving the foaming flood (of the world) is (one) lit up in Sahaj.
(For the one without the Name,) eating is poison, speaking is poison, (he) does the work of poison;
bound at Jam's door, (such people) are beaten; (one) will be freed (only) by the True Name.
As (one) came, so (empty-handed) will (one) go, taking along what was done, written down.
The manmukh has lost (even his) capital, and receives punishment in the (Lord's) court.
The world is counterfeit, the True One is pure: reflect (on this) through the Guru's Shabad.
Rare are the people known to have within them the knowledge of Murari (the Lord).
(One who) bears the unbearable (blow), (within him) the spring of the immortal One, whose form is bliss, begins to flow.
Nanak is the fish (of) the water; (O God,) if it pleases you, keep (this) love (in me). ॥5॥
1331.2: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Songs and music, delights and cleverness,
joys and revels, the giving of orders — none of these,
nor dress and food, do I take into my mind;
through the Naam I make truth, Sahaj and peace dwell (within).
What do I know of what (the Lord) does and causes all to be done?
Without the Naam nothing pleases (my) body.
The wonders of yoga, relish and bliss (for me are)
devotion to Gobind (the Lord of the universe), held in the mind with true love;
(his) praise is my own deed and work;
within (me) the Sovereign, radiant as the sun, is pervading.
The love of the Beloved, the Beloved, I have lovingly held in my heart;
(he is) the Master of the meek, (my) Husband, Banwari (the Lord).
Day and night the Naam is (my) giving and (my) keeping of vows;
as I reflect on the essence (the Lord), the waves (of the mind) are sated.
(O God,) what power have I to tell of the Untellable?
I worship (you only as) you make me worship.
(When the Lord) dwells within, the sense of I and mine ends.
Whom (else) should I serve? There is no other at all.
The Guru's Shabad is the supreme relish, sweet;
such Amrit have I seen within.
Whoever has tasted it attains the perfect state;
O Nanak, (he) is sated, and (his) body is at peace. ॥5॥
1331.3: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Seeing (the Lord) within, through the Shabad the mind is won over; there is no other who can dye (it with love).
Day and night (the Lord) watches over beings and cares for them; the rule is his alone.
My God is deep in colour and exceedingly beautiful;
merciful to the meek, the Beloved, the enticer of the mind, full of sweetness, a deep crimson.
The well (of Amrit) is high above; the sky (the awareness risen high) is the water-drawer, (and so one becomes) the drinker of Amrit.
He whose creation it is knows its way; through the Guru (this) knowledge is reflected on.
The ray (of the Light) has spread, the lotuses (of the heart) have blossomed in delight; the sun has merged in the house of the moon.
Destroying death (its dread), desire has been slain in the mind; by the Guru's grace God has been found.
(The tongue) is dyed in the deep crimson of utmost delight; there is no other colour.
O Nanak, (those) dyed (in love) by savouring (the Name) with the tongue find that same God pervading (everywhere). ॥4॥
1332.1: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Raval yogis waste away in (their) twelve (orders), the sannyasis in (their) ten;
yogis, the patch-robed and the hair-pluckers: without the Shabad, (all have) the noose round the neck.
Those dyed in the Shabad are the perfect Bairagis (the truly detached);
(they) have begged alms of the (Lord) who dwells in the heart, (and their) attention is fixed in love of the One.
Brahmins read (scriptural) debate, perform rituals, and have (others) perform rites;
without understanding (they) see nothing; the manmukh, separated (from the Lord), suffers pain.
Those joined to the Shabad are pure in conduct; in the True Court (they) are honoured.
Day and night (their) attention stays on the jewel of the Name; age after age (they) remain merged in the True One.
All rites and duties, purity and restraint, chanting, austerity and pilgrimage dwell in the Shabad.
O Nanak, (the one who), united (by the Lord), meets the True Guru: (his) sorrows, sins and death flee. ॥4॥
1332.2: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(With) the dust (of the feet) of the Sants (saints), the company of the holy, and the Lord's praise, swim across (the world-ocean).
What can poor Jam do? (He) is afraid, (when) through the Guru Murari dwells in the heart.
Let life without the Naam burn away.
O mind, I chant the Lord's chant, (that is my) rosary; through the Guru (its) relish comes.
One who has the true peace of the Guru's teaching — what praise of him can be told?
Rubies, jewels, gems and treasures: seeking, one finds them through the Guru.
(He) recognises (divine) knowledge, and meditation is (his) true wealth; (he) fixes his attention on the Shabad of the One,
and is rapt in meditation on the One who needs no support, no food, untouched (by Maya), without fear.
(His) seven seas are filled with pure water; (he) floats the boat turned back (from the world).
(He) holds back the (mind) running outward and keeps it (within); through the Guru (he) merges in Sahaj.
He is the householder, he the servant (of God) and renunciate, who through the Guru has recognised his own self.
Says Nanak, (for one whose) mind is won over by the True Shabad, there is no other at all. ॥5॥
1332.3: Raag Prabhati, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Rare is one who understands through the Guru; (such a one) stays merged (in God) through the Shabad;
dyed in the Naam, (he) ever finds peace and keeps his attention fixed on the True One.
Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, O brothers.
By the Guru's grace the mind is made steady; day and night it stays filled with the Lord's essence.
Every day, day and night, practise devotion; this is what is gained in this age, O brother.
(God's) servants are ever pure, no filth clings (to them); (they) fix (their) minds on the True Name.
The True Guru has shown (me) the adornment of peace; in the Naam is great glory.
The inexhaustible storehouses are full, never do they run short; ever serve the Lord, O brother.
The one to whom the Creator himself gives (it), in his mind (the Name) comes to dwell.
O Nanak, ever meditate on the Naam; the True Guru has shown (it). ॥4॥
1333.1: Raag Prabhati, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Forgive (me), the one without virtue, O Master, and unite (me with you) yourself.
You are endless, your end has not been found; through the Shabad make (me) understand.
O dear Lord, I am a sacrifice to you.
(My) body and mind I offer, I lay (them) before you; may I ever remain in (your) refuge.
Keep (me) ever within your will, O Master; give (me) the Lord's Name alone, (that is my) glory.
From the perfect Guru (your) will is known, and night and day one merges in Sahaj.
In your will is devotion, if it pleases you; you yourself forgive and unite (us).
In your will (I) have found lasting peace; the Guru has quenched the fire of craving.
What you do, O Creator, that alone happens; nothing else can be done.
O Nanak, there is no other giver as great as the Naam; (it) is found from the perfect Guru. ॥4॥
1333.2: Raag Prabhati, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have praised the Lord through the Guru have, by praising, come to know the Lord;
the doubt of duality has gone from within (them); through the Guru's Shabad (they) have recognised (him).
O dear Lord, you are that One, my only one.
I repeat (your Name), I praise you alone; liberation and wisdom come from you.
Those who praise (you) through the Guru find the relish; sweet is the Amrit, the best of all.
Ever sweet, never insipid, is reflection through the Guru's Shabad.
He who has made (it) taste sweet alone knows (it); to him I am a sacrifice.
Through the Shabad I ever praise the Giver of peace, and rid myself of self within.
My True Guru is ever the Giver; whatever fruit one desires, that fruit one obtains.
O Nanak, (one who) receives the Naam receives glory; through the Guru's Shabad (one) finds the True One. ॥4॥
1333.3: Raag Prabhati, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who are in your refuge, O dear Lord, you are able to protect.
I can think of no other as great as you; there has been none, nor will there be.
O dear Lord, (may I) ever (stay) in your refuge.
As it pleases you, so protect (me), my Master; this is your greatness.
Those who are in your refuge, O dear Lord, you cherish.
In mercy you yourself protect (them), O dear Lord; Jamkaal (death) cannot touch (them).
Your refuge is true, O dear Lord; it neither lessens nor passes away.
One who leaves the Lord and clings to the love of another is born and dies.
Those who are in your refuge, O dear Lord, have no pain or hunger at all.
O Nanak, ever praise the Naam; (so) you will merge in the True Shabad. ॥4॥
1334.1: Raag Prabhati, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through the Guru, ever meditate on the dear Lord as long as there is life and breath.
(The one whose) mind has become pure through the Guru's Shabad, (whose) pride of mind has ended,
fruitful is the life of that mortal; (he) has merged in the Lord's Name.
O my mind, one should hear the Guru's teaching:
the Lord's Name ever gives peace; one should drink the Lord's essence in Sahaj.
Those who recognise (their) source dwell in their own home (within), and peace comes in Sahaj.
Through the Guru's Shabad the lotus (of the heart) has blossomed, and Haumai (ego) and evil-mindedness are lost.
In all, the One True Lord is at work; rare is one who understands (this).
(One whose) mind has become pure through the Guru's teaching utters the Amrit, the essence (the Lord);
the Lord's Name has come to dwell in (his) mind for ever; within the mind itself the mind is won over.
(I) am ever a sacrifice to my Guru, through whom (one) recognises Ram, the Soul pervading all.
(One who) in the human birth has not served the True Guru has wasted (his) life in vain.
If (the Lord) casts (his) glance of grace, then (he) brings (one) to the True Guru, and (one) merges, with ease, in Sahaj.
O Nanak, (one who) receives the Naam receives glory; (he) has meditated (on it) by perfect fortune. ॥4॥
1334.2: Raag Prabhati, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(God) himself makes the many-coloured kinds (of beings); creating the world, God has staged (this) play.
Making and making, (he) watches over (it); (he) does and causes to be done; (he) has given sustenance to all beings.
In the time of Kalyug Ram is pervading (all);
the One God fills every heart; through the Guru the Name of the Lord, Har Har, is revealed.
Hidden, the Naam is at work in Kalyug; the Lord fills every heart to the brim.
The jewel of the Name has shone forth in the hearts of those who have run to the Guru's refuge.
(One who) brings the five senses, all five, under control, and through the Guru's teaching gains forgiveness and contentment,
blessed, blessed is that servant of the Lord, great and perfect, who sings the Lord's praises in reverent fear and Bairag (longing for the Lord).
If anyone turns (his) face from the Guru and does not keep the Guru's word in mind,
(though) performing rites (he) amasses much wealth, whatever (he) does, (he) falls into hell.
The One Word and the One God are at work; all creation proceeds from the One alone.
O Nanak, (one whom the Lord) unites in union through the Guru goes and blends, through the Guru, in the Lord, Har Har. ॥5॥
1334.3: Raag Prabhati, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O my mind, praise your Guru.
If perfect fortune is (written) on (your) face and forehead, ever immerse (yourself) in the Lord's virtues.
The Lord gives the food of the Name that is Amrit;
among millions, rare is one who receives (it),
(the one) on whom (the Lord) casts his own glance of grace.
Enshrine the Guru's feet in (your) mind,
(and) pain and darkness go from within,
(and) the True One himself unites (you with himself).
Give your love to the Guru's Bani;
here and hereafter this is the support;
(The one whom) the True One makes accept his will,
he alone is the devotee, graceful and wise;
Nanak is ever a sacrifice to him. ॥4॥
1335.1: Raag Prabhati Bibhas, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Through the Guru's teaching we sing (God's) virtues, savouring them again and again; in the state of unman (the mind raised above the world) (our) attention is fixed on the Name.
Through the Guru's Shabad (we) have drunk the essence that is Amrit; we are a sacrifice to the Name.
The Lord, life of the world, is our very breath.
The sublime Lord has become dear within (our) hearts, (since) the Guru gave the mantra of the Lord into (our) ears.
Come, O Sants, my brothers, come together; gathered, let us tell of the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
By what means, how should one find one's own God? Give me, as alms, the teaching of the Lord.
The Lord, Har Har, dwells in the Sat Sangat (the company of the true); meeting in the Sangat, one comes to know the Lord's virtues.
By great good fortune (we) have found the Sat Sangat; touching the Guru, the True Guru, (we) have found the Lord.
We sing the virtues of God, the unreachable Master; singing (his) virtues, we are lost in wonder.
The Guru has shown mercy to servant Nanak, and in an instant has given (him) the Lord's Name as alms. ॥4॥
1335.2: Raag Prabhati, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
When the sun rises, the Gurmukhs speak (the Name of) the Lord, and all night long they keep the Lord's words in mind.
My God has set this longing in me (too); I (too) search for God, the Lord.
My mind has become the dust of the feet of the Saadh (the Guru).
The Guru has made the sweet Name of the Lord, Har Har, firm (in me); with my hair I dust the Guru's feet.
For the Saakat (one who has turned from God) day and night are dark; (Saakats) are caught in attachment, in the net of Maya.
Not for a moment, not for an instant, has the Lord God dwelt in (their) hearts; in many ways they are bound in debt, every hair of them.
(Those who), joining the Sat Sangat, have gained wisdom and understanding are freed from the nets of Haumai and of possessiveness.
The Lord's Name, the Lord himself, has come to taste sweet (to them); through the Shabad the Guru has filled (them) with joy.
We are (your) children, O Guru, O unreachable Master; O Guru, in mercy cherish (us).
Says Nanak, O God, O Guru, O Gopal (the Lord who sustains all), pull out (your) children, drowning in the poisonous world-ocean. ॥4॥
1335.3: Raag Prabhati, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord God showed mercy for a single instant, and (they) sang (his) virtues, savouring them, steeped in delight.
Those who through the Guru drank (the essence of) the Lord even for an instant, singing and hearing, both have been set free.
In my mind the essence of the Name of Ram, Har Har, has settled.
Through the Guru (I) have found the cool water of the Naam; (I) have drunk the essence of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in deep draughts.
Those in whose hearts love of the Lord has taken hold bear a bright mark on their foreheads.
The glory of the Lord's servants spreads over all the world, as the moon (shines) among the stars.
Those in whose hearts the Lord's Name has not come to dwell: all their works are insipid,
as when a man adorns (his) body (but has no nose); without the Name (people) are noseless, their noses cut off.
In every heart the beloved Ram, the Sovereign, is pervading; the One is at work everywhere, within all.
The Lord has shown mercy to servant Nanak, and through the Guru's word (he) has meditated (on the Lord) moment by moment. ॥4॥
1336.1: Raag Prabhati, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
God, the unreachable, the merciful, showed mercy, and we uttered with our mouths the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
(We) meditated on the Name of the Lord, purifier of the fallen, and all sins and wrongs were washed away.
O mind, repeat the Name of Ram, who pervades all.
(Whoever) has sung of the One merciful to the meek, the destroyer of sorrow, has found through the Guru's teaching the treasure of the Naam.
The Lord dwells in the town of every body; with understanding from the Guru's teaching, the Lord, Har Har, is known for certain.
(One in whose) pool of the body the Lord's Name has shone forth has found the Lord God in (his own) house, in the temple (of the heart).
The men who wander and wander in the wilderness: those foolish Saakats are plundered,
as the fragrance (of musk) dwells in the deer's navel, yet it roams and roams, seizing at the bushes.
O God, you are great and unreachable, too deep for understanding to fathom; give (me) the understanding (by which), O Lord God, (I may) find (you).
The Guru has placed (his) hand on servant Nanak's head, and he stays absorbed in the Name of the Lord, Ram. ॥4॥
1336.2: Raag Prabhati, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Love for Ram's Name has taken hold in (my) mind; (I) have repeated (the Name of) the great Lord God, Har Har;
the True Guru's words have brought peace to (my) heart; the Lord God has shown mercy.
O my mind, dwell on the Name of Ram, the Lord, every moment.
The perfect Guru has given the gift of the Lord, Har Har; the Lord's Name has come to dwell in mind and body.
(The Lord) dwells in the town of the body, in the house, in the temple (of the heart); repeating (the Name) through the Guru, (his servants) sing (his) glory.
In this world and the next (the Lord's) servants are at ease; (their) faces are bright, and through the Guru (they) cross over.
Attention is fixed on the fearless Lord, Har Har Har; in an instant the Guru has set the Lord in (my) heart.
All the faults of (his) servant, from millions upon millions (of births), the Lord has removed in a single moment.
It is from you alone, O God, that your servants are known; (those who) have known God become foremost among (your) servants.
The Lord, Har Har, has placed himself within the Lord's servants; servant Nanak and the Lord God are one. ॥4॥
1337.1: Raag Prabhati, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Guru, the True Guru, has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, firm (in us); we were dead, and repeating (the Name of) the Lord we have come alive.
Blessed, blessed is the Guru, the perfect Guru, the True Guru, (who), giving (his) arm, has drawn out those drowning in the poison.
O mind, repeat Ram's Name; worship (him).
By whispered spells and such devices (God) is found nowhere; through the perfect Guru the Lord God is found.
The essence of Ram's Name is Ram's elixir (the home of every relish); through the Guru's teaching (I) have drunk this essence and delighted in it.
Joining the Sangat, even slag iron (manoor) becomes gold; the Guru has set the Lord in the heart.
(Those who) are ever lured by Haumai and by greed for poisonous Maya, entangled in attachment to sons and wife,
have never served the feet of the Sants; those manmukhs stay full of the smouldering ash (of craving).
Your virtues, O God, you alone know; worn out, we have fallen into your refuge.
As you know best, so keep (us), O Master; servant Nanak is your slave.
1337.2: Raag Prabhati Bibhas, Partal, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the treasure (of all).
(By it) you will receive honour in the Lord's court.
All who have repeated (the Name) have crossed to the far shore.
Hear, O mind: fix your attention on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Hear, O mind: the Lord's praise is the bath at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.
Hear, O mind: through the Guru you will receive honour.
O mind, repeat (the Name of) the Supreme God, the foremost of all.
In an instant he destroys millions of sins.
O Nanak, meet the Lord God. ॥2॥
1337.3: Raag Prabhati Bibhas, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Lord who made (your) mind and fashioned all (your) body,
who formed (it) of the five elements and graced (it) with (his) Light,
(who gave) the earth for a bed, and water for (your) use:
do not forget (him) for a moment; serve Saringpani.
O mind, by serving the True Guru the supreme state is reached.
(If) you stay apart from joy and grief, then you will find the Lord of (your) life.
(He who) has given you clothes, pleasures and countless relishes to enjoy,
who made mother, father and all the family,
who brings sustenance (to all) in water and on land, O friend:
serve that Lord, ever and always.
He is a companion there where there is no one;
in an instant he washes away millions of wrongs.
He gives (his) gifts and does not regret (them);
once he forgives, he never calls (one to account) again.
By the joining of past deeds (I) have searched (him) out and found (him);
Gopal dwells in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy).
Meeting the Guru, (we) have come to your door, (O God);
O Murari, grant servant Nanak the sight of you. ॥4॥
1338.1: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Service of God is the glory of (his) servant;
his lust, anger and greed are wiped away.
(O God,) your Name is in the storehouse of (your) servant;
(your servants) sing (your) virtues in love of the sight of God.
O God, devotion to you you yourself have made known (to them);
cutting the rope (of Maya), you have set (your) servants free.
The servant who is dyed in the colour of God's love
has found peace in the company of God.
Only one who has tasted this relish knows it;
seeing it again and again, he is filled with wonder in his mind.
He is at peace, he is the highest of all,
in whose heart that God has come to dwell.
He alone is steadfast; he does not come and go (in birth and death);
day and night he sings the virtues of the Lord God.
Bow, all of you, to him
in whose mind is the perfect Formless One.
Show mercy to me, O Master, O Divine One,
that Nanak may be saved by serving (your) servants. ॥4॥
1338.2: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Singing (God's) virtues, bliss arises in the mind;
at all hours I remember the Lord.
The (Guru) through whose (gift of) remembrance sins depart:
at the feet of that Guru we fall.
O beloved Sant (the Guru), give (me) good understanding,
that I may remember the Naam, (which) carries me across.
The Guru who has told (us) the straight path,
(by whom the mind), forsaking all, is enthralled by the Lord's Name:
to that Guru one should ever be a sacrifice,
the Guru from whom remembrance of the Lord is received.
The Guru who has carried drowning mortals across,
by whose grace Maya cannot lure,
the Guru who has set right this world and the next:
to that Guru I am ever a sacrifice.
From a great fool (the Guru) has made (me) wise;
the story of the perfect Guru cannot be told.
O Nanak, the Guru, the Divine One, is (one with) Paarbrahm (the Supreme Lord);
by great good fortune the Lord's service is found. ॥4॥
1338.3: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
All sorrows are wiped away; (God) has given peace and had (me) repeat his own Name;
in mercy (he) has set (me) to his service and wiped out all wrongdoing.
We, children, are in the refuge of merciful God.
Cutting away (our) faults, God has made (us) his own; my Guru, Gopal, has saved (us).
Torments and sins were destroyed in an instant, (when) the Master became merciful.
With every breath I worship the Supreme Lord, and am a sacrifice to my True Guru.
The Master is unreachable, beyond the senses, endless; his end cannot be found.
Earning the profit (of the Name), one becomes rich; one should meditate on one's own God.
At all hours I meditate on the Supreme Lord; ever and ever (I) have sung (his) virtues.
Says Nanak, my hopes are fulfilled; (I) have found the Guru, (one with) the Supreme Lord. ॥4॥
1339.1: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering the Naam, all sins are destroyed;
the Guru has given the True Name as capital.
(God's servants) are honoured in God's court;
serving (him), the servants are ever beautiful.
O my brothers, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
(By it) all ailments and all faults are destroyed, and the darkness of ignorance leaves the mind.
The Guru has saved (us) from birth and death, O friend;
love for the Lord's Name has taken hold.
The sufferings of millions of births are gone;
whatever pleases him will be good.
I am ever a sacrifice to that Guru,
by whose grace I meditate on the Lord's Name.
Such a Guru is found by great good fortune,
meeting whom, the attention is fixed on Ram.
Show mercy, O Supreme Lord, O Master;
you know the inner being of every heart.
At all hours keep (me) attuned to you;
servant Nanak is in God's refuge. ॥4॥
1339.2: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those whom God in mercy has made his own
(he) has given the Lord's Name to repeat.
Singing the virtues of Gubind at all hours,
(their) fears are destroyed and all anxiety is lifted.
Clinging to the True Guru's feet, (they) are saved;
what the Guru says, that alone is good and sweet (to them), as they give up the mind's own counsel.
That Lord God has come to dwell in mind and body;
no strife, no suffering, no obstacle at all arises.
Ever and always God is with the soul;
in the colour of the Name (the mind's) filth is washed away.
Love for (the Lord's) lotus feet has taken hold;
lust, anger and pride are destroyed.
The way to meet God is known;
through love and devotion the mind is won over to the Lord.
Hear, O friend, O Sant, O companion who brings peace:
the Lord's Name is a jewel, beyond grasp and beyond weighing;
one should ever and always sing of God, the treasure of virtues;
Says Nanak, (this) is found by great good fortune. ॥4॥
1339.3: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
They are the wealthy, they the true bankers,
(who) have bought the Naam (as their wares) for the Lord's court.
O mind, my friend, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
The perfect Guru is found by great good fortune; (his) way is pure and complete.
(I) have gained the profit; songs of rejoicing ring out;
by the grace of the Sant (the Guru) I sing the Lord's virtues.
The birth is made fruitful, the life approved;
by the Guru's grace, delight in the Lord's love.
Lust, anger and pride are destroyed.
O Nanak, through the Guru (they) cross over. ॥4॥
1339.4: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Perfect is the Guru, perfect his power;
the Guru's Shabad stands unshaken for ever and ever.
One in whose mind the Guru's Bani dwells:
all his pain and sorrow flee.
Dyed in the Lord's love, the mind sings Ram's virtues;
he is free who bathes in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh (the Guru).
By the Guru's grace (they) have crossed over;
(their) fear, doubt and vices are destroyed;
within (their) minds and bodies the Guru's feet have come to dwell;
the Saadhs are fearless; (they) have fallen into the Lord's refuge.
(Within them are) bliss, Sahaj, delight and peace in abundance;
no enemy, no sorrow comes near (them).
The perfect Guru has made (them) his own and kept (them) safe;
repeating the Lord's Name, all (their) sins have fallen away.
The Sants, the friends and the Sikhs are at ease;
the perfect Guru has brought (them) and united (them) with God.
(He) has cut the noose of the pain of birth and death;
says Nanak, the Guru has drawn a veil (over them) and covered (their honour). ॥4॥
1340.1: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One to whom) the perfect True Guru has given the Naam
(has) bliss, joy, well-being and lasting peace; (his) every task is accomplished.
(One in whose) mind the Guru's lotus feet have come to dwell:
(his) sorrow, pain and false doubts are destroyed.
Rising every day, sing God's Bani;
remember the Lord at all hours, O mortals.
At home and outside, God is in every place;
wherever I go, he is with me as my helper.
that Nanak may ever repeat (the Name of God), the treasure of virtues. ॥4॥
1340.2: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord God is skilful and wise;
The perfect Guru is found by great good fortune; one should be a sacrifice to (his) sight.
(The Guru) has erased sins through the Shabad, (and granted) contentment;
(one) has become fit to worship the Naam.
In the Saadh Sangat light has dawned (within),
and the lotus feet (of the Lord) have come to dwell in the mind.
He who made (us) has saved (us);
perfect is God, the Master of the masterless.
One whom he graces in mercy:
his deeds and conduct are made complete.
He sings (God's) virtues day after day, ever new;
he does not wander through the eighty-four lakh forms of life.
Here and hereafter (his) feet are worshipped;
(his) face is bright in the True Court.
One on whose forehead the Guru has placed (his) hand:
such a servant is rare, one among millions;
he sees (God) filling the water, the land and the sky.
O Nanak, through the dust (of the feet) of such a servant (you) will be saved. ॥4॥
1340.3: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
To my perfect Guru I am a sacrifice,
by whose grace the chant of the Lord, Har Har, is chanted.
Hearing (his) Bani, which is Amrit, (the mind) is filled with joy,
and the entanglements of Maya are destroyed.
Love for the True Shabad has taken hold,
and my own Lord God has come into (my) mind.
Repeating the Naam, light has dawned (within);
through the Guru's Shabad (God) has made his dwelling in the heart.
The Guru is all-powerful, ever merciful;
O Nanak, repeating the Lord again and again, (they) are filled with joy. ॥4॥
1341.1: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeating Guru, Guru, (I) have found lasting peace.
(God), merciful to the meek, became kind and himself had (me) repeat his own Name.
Joining the company of the Sants, light has dawned (within);
repeating the Lord, Har Har, (my) hope is fulfilled.
All blessings and comforts have come to dwell in the mind;
(I) have sung the Lord's virtues, (for), O Nanak, the Guru has been pleased. ॥2॥
1341.2: Raag Prabhati Bibhas, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
There is no other place (of shelter),
(In it are) all spiritual powers and every blessing;
One should repeat the Lord's Name always;
(so) lust, anger and pride are destroyed, and love for the One takes hold.
(One who) is joined to the Name, (his) sorrow flees; (God) is able to cherish (whoever comes to his) refuge.
He meets the True Guru, and Jam does not press him, whose meeting is ordained from the very source.
Meditating night and day on the Lord, Har Har, give up the doubts of the mind.
In the Saadh Sangat the Lord is met by one whose fortune is full.
The troubles of birth after birth are destroyed; (God) himself has saved (them).
(He is) mother, father, friend and brother; O servant Nanak, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
1341.3: Raag Prabhati Bibhas, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Repeat (the Name of) the all-pervading Ram, Ram, Ram.
(so) strife and suffering, greed, attachment and the fever of ego are destroyed.
Give up self and cling to the feet of the Sants; (so) the mind is made pure and sins depart.
Nanak is a child and knows nothing; to protect (him), God is mother and father. ॥2॥
1341.4: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The refuge of (your) lotus feet is (my) support, (O God).
(You are) the Master, high, vast and endless; over all, you alone are the One.
(You are) the support of every life, the one who ends sorrow, the giver of discerning understanding.
Bow to the Protector; in the mind worship the one God.
Nanak bathes in the dust (of the feet) of the Sants; (one who does so) gains countless comforts. ॥2॥
1342.1: Raag Prabhati Bibhas, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Crazed double-mindedness has driven the mind mad;
in false greed (one) has wasted (one's) life.
(Double-mindedness) clings on, and no dam is set (against it);
making the Naam firm (within them), the True Guru has saved (them).
Neither does the mind die, nor does Maya die.
He who made all this alone knows (its secret); reflecting on the Shabad, one crosses the fearsome (world-) ocean.
Amassing Maya, kings grow proud,
(but that) beloved Maya does not go with (them).
Attachment to Maya has many colours,
(but) without the Name there is no friend, no companion.
As (people) see (their own) mind, so (they take) the mind of others (to be).
As is the desire, so is the state.
As are (one's) deeds, so is the attention (one) fixes;
asking the True Guru, (one) finds the home of Sahaj.
Caught in melody and sound, the mind is in love of duality;
with deceit within, (one) suffers great pain.
When the True Guru is met, understanding comes,
(and one) keeps one's attention fixed on the True Name.
Through the True Shabad (he) lives the Truth,
through the True Bani he sings the Lord's virtues,
dwells in (his) own home and attains the immortal state;
then (he) wins glory at the True Door.
Without serving the Guru there is no devotion,
though one make countless efforts.
(One who) through the Shabad loses Haumai and the sense of mine:
in his mind alone the pure Name dwells.
In this world the Shabad is the most excellent work;
without the Shabad, all else is the pitch dark of attachment.
Through the Shabad (one) keeps the Naam enshrined in the heart;
through the Shabad come the high state, understanding and the door of liberation.
There is no other who makes and watches over (all);
the True One himself is beyond compare and without end.
Through Ram's Name the highest state is reached;
O Nanak, (only) a rare person seeks and finds (it). ॥8॥
1342.2: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Attachment to Maya has spread over the whole world.
Seeing a woman, (one) is lured by lust;
(one) has let love for sons and gold grow;
(one deems) everything one's own, and Ram alone a stranger.
Such is the chant I repeat, (and that is my) rosary:
setting aside pain and pleasure, (I offer) a devotion apart (from them).
O treasure of virtues, none has found your end.
Through the True Shabad (one) merges in you.
You yourself have set up the coming and going;
they alone are devotees who have fixed their minds on the True One.
Knowledge of Narhari, the Lord beyond desire, and meditation on him
no one knows without meeting the True Guru.
(His) Light pervades all the pools (of the bodies);
I am a sacrifice to the One whose form is bliss.
(One who) gains loving devotion through the Guru's teaching
burns Haumai out from within through the Shabad,
keeps the running (mind) safe, and holds it back and still;
and enshrines the True Name in the mind.
The wondrous amusements that make one heedless come to an end (for him);
through the Guru's teaching (his mind) is won over, and his attention is fixed on the One;
seeing (the Lord), (he) has quenched the fire (of craving) in the water (of the Naam).
He understands (this) who is greatly fortunate.
(One who) serves the True Guru puts an end to doubt,
stays awake night and day, and fixes his attention on the True One.
(He) knows the One alone, no other;
he serves the Giver of comfort and becomes pure.
Reflection on the Shabad is (his) service and (his) awareness;
killing Haumai is (his) jap, tap and self-discipline.
When (the Guru) lets (him) hear the Shabad, (he) is free while yet alive;
living truly, (he) finds true comfort.
The Giver of comfort is the One who wipes out pain;
no other, second task comes to (his) mind.
(He) has set body, mind and wealth before the Lord;
says Nanak, (he) has tasted the supreme essence. ॥8॥
1343.1: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(One) performs nivli karam, makes the bhuangam (channel) a furnace, and breathes out, breathes in and holds the breath (rechak, purak, kumbhak),
(but) without the True Guru there is no understanding at all; strayed in doubt, (one) drowns and dies.
The blind one, full (of filth), fills (the vessel) again and again and washes, but the filth within never comes off.
Without the Naam all deeds are hollow, like a juggler lost in the illusion (of his own show).
The Name of the Immaculate One is itself (my) six rites (khat karam);
you are the ocean of virtues; the faults are in me.
(The manmukh's) running about is for the business of Maya; through evil counsel (his) work is corrupt.
The fool makes much of himself, but cannot understand (the right) work.
(His) desire is in Maya the enticer; the manmukh is ruined by (his own) words.
The bathing of the vile one is false, and (his) fine adornments are hollow.
False is the counsel of (his) mind; (his) conduct is vain strife.
Within the false one is pride; he does not get the relish of the Master.
Without the Name, whatever else is done tastes insipid.
In the company of the wicked one is ruined; poison is in (their) mouths, and (their) life is in vain.
O you who stray in doubt, let none of you die (this way).
Serving the True Guru, there is comfort for ever.
Without the True Guru no one has gained liberation;
(such) come and go and die; (each) dies and passes away.
This body is made of the three qualities (of Maya);
sorrow and anguish take hold of it.
Serve him who has neither mother nor father,
(and) craving and self-conceit end from within.
Wherever I look, there he is;
(but) without meeting the True Guru there is no liberation.
The True One (held) in the heart: this is the most excellent deed;
all else is hypocrisy; (such) worship brings ruin.
Recognise the Shabad; only then does double-mindedness end;
know the One alone (to dwell) within the home and outside.
This is the (right) counsel: the Shabad is the most excellent;
in double-mindedness, ashes fall on one's head.
Praise (of the Lord) is the (true) deed; the Guru's teaching is the most excellent;
in the assembly of the Sants, reflect on (the Lord's) virtues and on knowledge (of him).
(One who) subdues the mind: know (him) to be dead while living.
O Nanak, (such a one) is known and owned in the sight of the Gracious One. ॥8॥
1344.1: Raag Prabhati Dakhani, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Gautam was an ascetic, and Ahalya his wife; seeing her, Indra was lured.
(By Gautam's curse) a thousand marks of the yoni came upon his body; then he repented in his mind.
No one strays knowingly, O brother.
He alone strays whom (God) himself leads astray; he understands whom (God) makes understand.
Harichand, the king, lord of the earth, did not know the worth of what was written on the paper (of his destiny).
Had he known (it for) a fault, why would he have given such alms, and why been sold in the market?
On the pretext of the dwarf's form, (God) asked (Bali) for two and a half steps of earth.
Had Bali known that form, why would he go to the netherworld, why be deceived?
Vyas gave King Janmejay counsel, warned him and taught him;
(yet) holding the sacrifice, he had eighteen (Brahmins) slain: what past deeds have written cannot be turned aside.
I make no reckonings; I recognise (your) Hukam (God's will and command), and speak with love, as comes naturally.
Whatever comes to pass, I praise you alone; all is your greatness.
Through the Guru one stays untouched: no stain (of Maya) ever clings, and one stays ever in (your) refuge.
The foolish manmukh does not think ahead; when pain strikes, he repents.
The Creator who made this creation himself does (all) and has (it) done.
O Lord, pride does not leave the soul; falling into pride, one is consumed.
Everyone is made to err; the Creator himself does not err.
O Nanak, release is through the True Name; by the Guru's grace a rare one is set free. ॥8॥
1344.2: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(For one whose) support is speaking and hearing the Naam,
the useless busyness (of Maya) falls away;
whereas the manmukh has lost (his) honour in duality.
without the Name I have no other (support).
Listen, O blind, foolish, ignorant mind:
coming and going, (one) feels no shame; without the Guru (one) drowns again and again.
In attachment to Maya this mind is destroyed.
When (this) Hukam was written from the source, to whom should one complain?
Only a rare one recognises through the Guru
(that) one bereft of the Name is not set free.
Wandering and wandering, (the soul) tosses through the eighty-four lakh (forms);
without understanding from the Guru, there is the noose of Jam.
From moment to moment this mind is (now) in the sky, (now) in the netherworld;
through the Guru, cherishing the Naam, (it) is set free.
When (God) himself calls, there is no delay;
(one who) dies through the Shabad lives at ease.
Without the Guru no one has understanding;
he (God) himself does (all) and has (it) done.
(One whose) strife (God) ends sings the Lord's virtues;
(he meets) the perfect True Guru, (and) stays merged in Sahaj.
Then (he) steadies this wavering mind,
and making Truth (his) conduct, does the work (of the Naam).
How can one defiled within be clean?
Rare is the one who washes (the mind) with the Shabad.
A (rare) one lives the Truth through the Guru,
and checks his coming and going and brings it to rest.
(For one whose) food and drink is the fear (of God), (that is) the best of comforts;
in the company of the Lord's servants (he) reaches the far shore.
(He) speaks the Truth, and love (for God) makes (him) speak it;
the Guru's Shabad is (for him) the most excellent deed.
The Lord's praise is (his) ritual, (his) dharam, (his) honour and (his) worship;
lust and anger (he) roasts in the fire.
When the Lord's essence was tasted, then the mind was drenched (in it);
Nanak humbly prays: there is no other, no second (like it). ॥8॥
1345.1: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Repeat Ram's Name: (this is) the worship within;
reflect on the Guru's Shabad, (and you will see that) there is no other, no second.
The One alone pervades every place.
(I) see no other: to whom should (I) make offerings?
(My) mind and body are before you, (my) soul is with you, (O God);
this is my prayer: keep (me) as it pleases you.
(One whose) tongue holds the Truth, (whose) tongue is steeped in the Lord's relish,
(he) will be set free in God's refuge, through the Guru's teaching.
Rituals and religious duties were made by my God;
(but he) has set the glory of the Naam above all rituals.
The four padaarath are in the True Guru's hands;
(in his refuge) the three are absorbed, and in the one (liberation) one is fulfilled.
Those to whom the True Guru has given liberation and meditation
have recognised the Lord's state and become eminent.
(Those to whom) the Guru has given understanding are cooled in mind and body;
God has honoured (them): who has ever told (their) worth?
Says Nanak, the Guru has given (me this) understanding:
without the Name no one has attained the high state. ॥8॥
1345.2: Raag Prabhati, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Some the perfect Guru has forgiven from the source; (he) has given (them) a true make.
Dyed in the Lord's colour, (they) bear the true colour for ever; (their) sorrows are forgotten, and (they) have won honour.
False is the cleverness of evil counsel;
it takes no time at all (for it) to perish.
Pain and suffering take hold of the manmukh; the manmukh's pain does not go.
(Those who) through the Guru have known the Giver of comfort and pain, (he) takes into (his) refuge and unites (with himself).
Devotion of the heart will not come from the manmukhs; crazed, (they) waste away in Haumai.
In a moment this mind is (now) in the sky, (now) in the netherworld, as long as (one) does not know the Shabad.
The world has grown hungry and thirsty; without finding the True Guru there is no fulfilment.
With ease Sahaj is found, comfort is gained, and (one) goes to the Lord's court robed in honour.
In the court the One alone is the Knower and the Seer; pure is the Guru's Bani.
(He) himself is the listener, and weighs the Truth; he himself knows the state beyond desire.
Water with its waves, fire and air: then the three together brought forth the world;
(God) gave them such might and cunning, (yet) by (his) Hukam has held them in check.
Rare in the world are such people, (whom God) has tested and placed in (his) treasury.
(They) have risen above caste and varna, and have put an end to possessiveness and greed.
Dyed in the Name, they are the pure places of pilgrimage; (they) have put an end to the pain and filth of Haumai.
Nanak washes the feet of those to whom, through the Guru, the True One is pleasing. ॥8॥
1346.1: Raag Prabhati Bibhas, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
By the Guru's grace, see: the Lord's temple (Har Mandar) is right with you.
One should search out the Lord's temple through the Shabad; cherish the Lord's Name.
O my mind, (one who) is dyed in the Shabad takes on the colour (of love);
true is (his) devotion, true (his) temple of the Lord, and true renown shines forth (for him).
This body is the Lord's temple; through the jewel of knowledge it is revealed.
The manmukhs do not know the Root; in (such) a person the Lord's temple does not come (to light).
The dear Lord (himself) fashioned the Lord's temple, and keeps it adorned by (his) Hukam.
What is written from the source must be lived out; no one can erase it.
(Those who) recognised the Shabad, in love with the True Name, have found comfort;
through the Shabad the Lord's temple is beautiful, a fortress of gold of the Infinite One.
This world is the Lord's temple; without the Guru (there is) pitch darkness.
The blind, ignorant manmukhs worship in love of duality.
Where the account is called for, neither body nor caste goes there.
Those dyed in the True One are saved; (those caught) in love of duality are wretched.
In the Lord's temple is the treasure of the Naam, (but) the foolish and ignorant do not understand.
(Those who) by the Guru's grace recognised (it) have enshrined the Lord in the heart.
Those who, taking on (love's) colour, are dyed in the Shabad have come to know the Guru's Bani from the Guru.
Holy, pure and spotless are those people, merged in the Lord's Name.
The Lord's temple is the Lord's shop, which (he) keeps adorned with the Shabad;
in it the one merchandise is the Naam; through the Guru (people) take it and adorn (their lives).
In the Lord's temple the mind is (mere) iron, enticed by love of duality;
on meeting the paaras (the Guru), it has become gold; its worth cannot be told.
In the Lord's temple the Lord dwells; he pervades all, through and through.
O Nanak, one should trade through the Guru; (then) the bargain is true. ॥11॥
1346.2: Raag Prabhati, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who are awake in the fear and love (of God) keep the (true) jagran, washing off the filth of Haumai.
They stay ever awake, guard their own house, and beat and drive out the five thieves.
O my mind, through the Guru meditate on the Naam;
the path by which the Lord is found: O mind, do those deeds alone.
Through the Guru the melody of Sahaj wells up, and the pain of Haumai goes from within.
The Name of the Lord, Har, dwells in the mind, as (one) sings the Lord's virtues in Sahaj.
Through the Guru's teaching, beautiful are the faces (of those who) have enshrined the Lord in the heart;
here and hereafter (they have) great comfort; repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, they have crossed over.
In Haumai there is no (true) jagran, and devotion to the Lord is not accepted.
The manmukhs find no shelter at the door (of the Lord), (for they) do (their) deeds in love of duality.
Cursed is the eating, cursed the wearing, of those who are in love with duality.
Worms of filth, steeped in filth, they die and are born, and come to ruin.
I am a sacrifice to those who have met the True Guru.
May I stay joined to their company, and remain merged in the True One alone.
The Guru is found by perfect fortune; by no (other) means can he be found.
From the True Guru Sahaj wells up, (and one) burns Haumai through the Shabad.
Hasten to the Lord's refuge, O my mind; (he) is able to do all.
O Nanak, may the Naam never be forgotten; whatever (God) does, that will come to be. ॥8॥
1347.1: Raag Prabhati Bibhas, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Mother, father, brother, son and wife
peck at their feed together with delight;
the mind is caught up in sweet attachment.
(But) those who buy (the Lord's) virtues are the support of my life.
The One alone is mine, the Knower of hearts.
The One is my mainstay, and on the One alone I lean; the great Being, the Master, is over the heads of kings.
My ties with the deceiving serpent (Maya) are broken;
the Guru has said (to me): she is false, a betrayer.
Sweet in the mouth, she turns bitter when eaten.
(My) mind is sated with the Amrit Name.
I have fallen out with greed and attachment;
the merciful Guru has set me free (from them).
This cheat has ruined many homes;
me the merciful Guru has saved.
With lust and anger I have made no league;
I have heard the Guru's teaching with my ears.
Wherever I look, there are these great vile ones (the passions);
my own Guru, Gopal, has saved (me).
I have made the ten women (the senses) forsaken wives;
the Guru has said (to me): through their pleasures these are a poisonous fire.
One who keeps ties with them goes down to the nether depths;
the Guru has saved me, attuning (me) to the Lord.
I have given up taking counsel with egotism;
the Guru has said (to me): it is a stubborn fool.
This homeless one finds a home nowhere;
the Guru has saved me, attuning (me to the Lord).
I have become the enemy of these people;
two cannot get on in one house.
Clinging to the hem (of the Guru), I have come before God (and prayed):
O all-knowing God, judge (between us).
God smiled and said: I have done justice;
(he) has set all the enemies to serve me;
you are the master; this whole house is yours.
Says Nanak, the Guru has settled (it). ॥8॥
1347.2: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the mind is anger and great pride;
(people) perform worship with great display;
(one) bathes and marks the body with (sacred) chakras,
(but) the filth within never goes.
No one has ever found God by this discipline;
(outside are) the marks of a Bhagauti, (but) the mind is enticed by Maya.
In the power of the five enemies, (they) commit sins, O brother;
bathing at a place of pilgrimage, they say all (their sins) are washed away;
fearless, they commit (them) again.
For (their) stains they are bound and taken to the city of Jam.
Tying on ankle bells, (they) beat the rhythm,
(but) with deceit within, they wander out of the beat.
Beating the snake's hole does not kill the snake.
God, who made you, knows everything.
(One who) warms himself at fires and (wears) ochre robes,
struck by misfortune, flees from home,
leaves his own land and wanders in foreign lands,
(yet) he has brought the five vile ones (lust and the rest) along with him.
He has his ears split (as a yogi), (yet) eyes the crumbs (of others);
he begs from door to door, and misses contentment.
Leaving his wife, he casts an evil eye on another's wife.
(God) is not found by garb; (the soul) is in great misery.
(One) does not speak, and sits as a silent sage (moni),
(but) with desire within, (he) is made to wander through births.
He abstains from grain and suffers pain in the body;
(but) he does not understand the Hukam, and possessiveness has him in its grip.
Without the True Guru, none has ever reached the highest state;
ask all the Vedas and Simritis.
The manmukh does (his) deeds in vain,
like a house of sand, which has no place to stand.
One on whom Gobind has been merciful
has tied the Guru's word into the hem of his robe.
Among millions, (only) some (such) Sant is seen;
Nanak has been carried across in their company.
If there is good fortune, the sight of (such a Sant) is gained;
(one) crosses over oneself, and the whole family is carried across. ॥2॥
1348.1: Raag Prabhati, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering the Naam, all sins are cut away;
the papers of Dharam Raj are torn up.
(One who), joining the Saadh Sangat, has found the Lord's essence:
the Supreme Lord has come to dwell in (his) heart.
Dwelling on Ram, on the Lord, Har Har, (he) has found comfort,
(who) has come to the refuge of the feet of your servants, (O Lord).
The going (from birth to birth) has ended, the darkness is dispelled;
the Guru has shown the door of liberation.
Mind and body are ever dyed in loving devotion to the Lord;
when God made (it) known, only then was (it) known.
He pervades within every heart;
without him there is no other.
Enmity, strife, fears and doubts are cut away;
God, the pure Soul, has himself done (this) righteous deed.
From the mighty waves (of the world, he) has reached the shore;
broken off for birth after birth, he is joined again.
(He) has cherished the Naam (as his) jap, tap and self-discipline;
his own Master has looked on (him) with grace.
Joy, comfort and well-being are there,
where the servants of Gopal, the Master of the world, are.
God, Gopal, has become well pleased (with them);
(their) being out of tune for birth after birth is wiped away.
Burnt offerings, sacrifices, austerities hanging upside down, worship,
and bathing at millions of places of pilgrimage (are all) accomplished
(when one) holds (God's) lotus feet in the heart (even) for an instant;
repeating Gobind, all tasks are accomplished.
Highest of the high is God's abode;
the Lord's servants fix their attention (on him) in Sahaj.
I long for the dust (of the feet) of the servants of (his) servants;
the Beloved, holder of every power, fills (all).
The Lord, the Beloved, is (my) mother and father, and near (me);
(you are my) friend and companion, (O God); my trust is in you.
Taking (them) by the hand, (you) have made your servants your own.
Nanak lives by repeating (your Name), O treasure of virtues. ॥8॥
1349.1: Raag Prabhati Bibhas, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(My) dread of dying and of living is gone,
(for the Lord,) in his own pleasure, has lit (in me) the light of Sahaj.
(His) Light has shone forth, and the darkness is dispelled;
reflecting (on him), (I) have found the jewel of Ram.
Where there is bliss, sorrow has fled far away;
(there) the mind, (become) a pearl, through its loving attention hides the Essence (the Lord, the root of all) within itself.
(O God,) whatever has come to pass is your will (Bhana);
one who understands it so is absorbed in Sahaj.
Says Kabir: (my) sins have wasted away,
(and my) mind is merged in the Life of the world. ॥4॥
1349.2: Raag Prabhati, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
If the one Allah dwells (only) in the mosque, then whose is the rest of the land?
The Hindus (hold that the Lord's) Name dwells in the idol; neither of the two has seen the Essence.
O Allah, O Ram, (grant) that I may live by your Name;
(The Hindu says) the Lord's abode is in the land to the south; (the Muslim, that) Allah's seat is in the west.
Search for (him) in the heart; search in the heart, the heart alone: this is (his) place, (his) seat.
The Brahmins keep the twenty-four ekadashis (the fasts of the eleventh lunar day); the Qazis, the month of Ramzan.
(They) put the eleven months aside, and (take) the treasure to be in the one alone.
What (is gained) by bathing at Orissa (at the shrine of Jagannath)? What by bowing the head in the mosque?
(If, with) deceit in the heart, (one) offers the namaz, what (is gained) by going on Hajj to the Kaaba?
(O God,) all these women and men that (you) have fashioned: all these are your forms.
Kabir is a little child of Ram-Allah; all the Gurus and the Pirs are my own.
Says Kabir: listen, O men and women: take the refuge of the One.
O mortal, repeat the Naam alone; only then will (you) surely cross over. ॥6॥
1349.3: Raag Prabhati, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
In the beginning Allah's Light brought forth (the world); all people are (the work) of (his) Kudrat (creative power).
From the one Light the whole world sprang up; (then) who are good, and who are bad?
O people, O brothers, do not go astray in doubt.
The Khaalik (Creator) is (the Lord) of the Khalak (creation), and within the creation is the Creator, filling every place.
From the one clay the Maker has shaped many kinds (of vessels);
there is no flaw in the vessels of clay, and no flaw in the potter.
The one True (Lord) alone is in all; by his doing all that is comes to be.
One who recognises (his) Hukam knows the One; him alone should one call (God's) banda (servant).
Allah is Alakh (beyond seeing) and cannot be seen; the Guru gave (me) the sweet molasses (of understanding him).
Says Kabir: my doubt is gone; (I) have seen the Niranjan (the One untouched by Maya) in all. ॥4॥
1350.1: Raag Prabhati, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Do not call the Vedas and the Kateb (the Semitic scriptures) false; false is (the one) who does not reflect (on them).
If (you) say that the one God (Khuda) is in all, then why kill the hen?
O Mullah, tell (me): (is this) the justice of God?
The doubt of your mind does not depart.
(You) seized the creature and brought it, (and) destroyed its body; (you) made (only) the clay bismil (slaughtered in the name of God).
(Its) light stays joined to the Imperishable, whose form is light; tell (me), what have (you) made halal?
What (is gained) by making (the body) clean with the wuzu (ablution) and washing the face? What by laying the head (to the ground) in the mosque?
If (you) offer the namaz with deceit in the heart, what (is gained) by going on Hajj to the Kaaba?
You are unclean; (you) have not grasped the Pure One; (you) have not known his secret.
Says Kabir: (you) have fallen short of paradise; (your) mind has taken to hell. ॥4॥
1350.2: Raag Prabhati, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
O Divine One, O mine of light, O Master, O Primal One, O all-pervading: the Sunn (the stillness where no worldly thought stirs) is your sandhya (the prayer at the junctures of the day).
The Siddhas in samadhi have not found (your) end; (they) stay clinging to (your) refuge.
O brothers, take up the aarti of the Immaculate Being (in this way): worship the True Guru.
Brahma stands pondering the Vedas, (yet) the Unseen One cannot be seen.
With the essence (of knowledge) made the oil and the Naam the wick, the light within the body is the lamp;
lit with the flame of the Lord of the world (Jagdish), (the lamp) is kindled; the one who understands, understands (it).
The five sounds (of every kind of instrument) ring out unstruck (sounding without being played), (and) Saringpani (the Lord) is with (me).
O Formless One, beyond desire, (your) servant Kabir has performed your aarti (thus). ॥3॥
1350.3: Raag Prabhati, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The pain of the mind the mind alone knows; or one should tell it before the One who understands.
I remember Ram, the Inner-knower; why should I have fear?
Gopal, the Lord of the world (Gosain), has pierced (my mind with his love);
In the mind (is his) shop, in the mind the town, in the mind (he is) the shopkeeper;
in the mind dwells the (Lord) of many forms, (yet) the worldly (one) wanders (outside).
(When) this mind was dyed in the Guru's Shabad, (its) double-mindedness was absorbed in Sahaj;
all is (his) Hukam, (and) he himself (gives) the Hukam; (such a one,) fearless, regards (all) alike.
Those who, knowing (him so), worship Purakhotam (the Supreme Being): the Unmanifest (Lord) is in their speech.
Says Nama: (they) have found the Life of the world, the Unseen, the Wondrous One, in the heart. ॥4॥
1351.1: Raag Prabhati, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
(He is) the source (of all), from the beginning of the ages, in every age; his end has not been known.
Ram pervades all, through and through; such is the form (of him) that is told.
Gobind thunders forth (and is manifest, where) the Shabad (of the Guru) resounds;
my dear Ram is bliss itself.
(As) the bawan sandalwood tree (the finest sandalwood) stands in the forest, (and) from (its) fragrance comfort comes (to all around),
(so the Lord) is the source of all, the source of every fragrance: (by his touch) common wood becomes sandalwood.
(O God,) you are the paaras, I am iron; in your company (I) have become gold.
You are merciful, the jewel, the ruby; Nama has merged in the True One. ॥3॥
1351.2: Raag Prabhati, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
The Being who has no lineage has made a play (of the world),
(and) within each and every body has hidden Brahm (himself).
No one knows the Light (that dwells) in beings,
(yet) whatever you and I do becomes known (to it).
As the pot is brought forth from clay,
(so) Bithal, the Lord, is himself the Maker (of all).
The bondage of (its own) deeds holds the soul fast;
(yet) whatever has been made, (the Lord) himself has made.
Namdev humbly prays: whatever this soul dwells upon, that it obtains;
(if it) abides ever in the all-pervading (Lord), it becomes immortal. ॥4॥
1351.3: Raag Prabhati, the hymn of Bhagat Beni Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(O hypocrite,) sandal on your body, (tulsi) leaves on your forehead,
(but) within the heart (it is as if) a knife (is held) in the palm of the hand;
the eye of a thug, the heron's (still) absorption;
to look at, (you are) a Vaishnav, (so still) as though the breath had fled from (your) mouth.
In Kalyug (you) bow long before Bhagwan (in the image),
(but your) gaze is cruel, and night (and day you are) steeped in strife.
Every day (you) bathe the body,
(keep) two dhotis, (perform) the rites, (take only) milk in (your) mouth;
(but) in the heart a knife is drawn and aimed,
(and) the habit is to take away others' wealth.
(You) worship the stone, (put on) the marks of Ganesh,
keep awake at night, entering into devotion,
dance with (your) feet, (but your) mind is on evil deeds;
O lecher, this dance (of yours) is unrighteous.
A deerskin seat, a rosary of tulsi,
with clean hands the tilak on the forehead,
falsehood in the heart, rudraksh (beads) at the throat:
O lecher, (you) do not utter (the Name of) Krishna (the Lord).
One who has not recognised the essence of the self:
all the religion of (such) a blind one is hollow.
Says Beni: (one who) meditates through the Guru (finds the way);
without the True Guru one does not find the way. ॥5॥
